statement: The Kitchen example releases streamlines from starting positions defined by a straight-line rake and uses many simultaneous streamlines to inspect flow-field features.
The Kitchen laboratory documentation identifies ke as turbulent kinetic energy, ep as turbulent dissipation rate, and the c-prefixed scalar fields as gas concentrations in this room-flow dataset.

Turbulent kinetic energy and turbulent dissipation rate are distinct standard turbulence quantities, so extrema of either field are scientifically distinct local turbulence-activity operationalizations.

Statistical spread of concentration is a scientifically meaningful way to describe mixture heterogeneity; normalized concentration spread supports a scale-independent comparison among concentration fields.

The Kitchen evidence supports reporting the selected concentration-field identity and a scientifically meaningful heterogeneity or distributional characterization; exact benchmark values come from execution.
